comment: The 9.5% is a peak, about 33 million watching at once. The 26.1% for Bulls-Jazz is about 72 million people who watched any part of Game 6, not a peak (the average was about 35.9 million). Two different measures, so the gap looks far bigger than it was.
The show never says or hints that Penny was a prostitute. She is a struggling waitress and actress who often fell behind on rent. A joke fan theory presented as something the show implied.
No report that Israel shot down a B-52. The only B-52 loss around that date was a crash on a test flight near Edwards Air Force Base, which officials did not attribute to any attack.
A prayer-chain message that has circulated since August 2010. Fact-checkers found no news report of such an accident, and names and places change between versions.
Steam's DRM wrapper is optional, and many Steam games run without the Steam client. Offline Mode has no fixed 30-day re-login rule, so 'all your games break in 30 days' is overstated.

No country automatically cancels a person's debts when they enter a mental institution. Debts can be contested in some cases, for example when a contract was signed without mental capacity, but they are not wiped out.

Presented as a real event, but it comes from an unverified 'Oreogate' group chat posted by an Instagram creator who set it to AI-generated songs. ABC notes none of the messages are verified, and the coverage does not support the lunchbox search.
On 29 January 2026 the Senate Foreign Relations Committee voted on the bill, but the full Senate held no vote that day. No floor vote is recorded.
Presents folklore as fact. The escape-route maps come mainly from Colombian oral tradition with no documentary evidence, and the stories of hiding rice or seeds in braids are Maroon oral legends.
The quote is real, but Zuckerberg said it on the Lex Fridman podcast in June 2023, not in August 2026. Labelling a three-year-old clip 'JUST IN' presents old remarks as new.
